message.content:
Based on my search, here is a comprehensive overview of the bones of the head:

## Overview

The human skull consists of **22 bones** (or 29 if including the inner ear bones and hyoid bone). These bones are primarily connected by immovable fibrous joints called **sutures**, with one exception—the mandible, which forms a movable synovial joint with the temporal bone.

The skull is divided into two main parts:
- **Neurocranium (Cranium)** – the protective case around the brain
- **Viscerocranium (Facial Skeleton)** – the bones that form the face

---

## The Cranium (Neurocranium) – 8 Bones

The cranium protects the brain, meninges, and cerebral vasculature. It can be subdivided into the cranial roof (calvaria) and cranial base.

| Bone | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Frontal bone** (1) | Forms the forehead and anterior portion of the skull roof; contains frontal sinuses; forms superior part of eye sockets |
| **Parietal bones** (2) | Form the sides and roof of the cranial vault; meet at the sagittal suture |
| **Occipital bone** (1) | Forms the back and base of the skull; contains the **foramen magnum** where the spinal cord passes through |
| **Temporal bones** (2) | Form the sides and base of the cranium; house structures of the middle and inner ear; contain the mastoid process and styloid process |
| **Sphenoid bone** (1) | Butterfly-shaped bone at the base of the skull; contains the sella turcica (houses pituitary gland); articulates with almost every other cranial bone |
| **Ethmoid bone** (1) | Located between the orbits; forms part of the nasal cavity; contains the cribriform plate for olfactory nerves |

### Major Cranial Sutures:
- **Coronal suture** – between frontal and parietal bones
- **Sagittal suture** – between the two parietal bones
- **Lambdoid suture** – between parietal and occipital bones
- **Squamous suture** – between parietal and temporal bones

---

## The Facial Skeleton (Viscerocranium) – 14 Bones

| Bone | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Mandible** (1) | The lower jaw; largest and strongest facial bone; only movable bone of the skull; houses lower teeth |
| **Maxillae** (2) | Form the upper jaw; contribute to the hard palate, nasal cavity, and orbits; contain maxillary sinuses |
| **Zygomatic bones** (2) | Form the cheekbones and part of the lateral walls of the orbits |
| **Nasal bones** (2) | Form the bridge of the nose |
| **Lacrimal bones** (2) | Small bones in the medial walls of the orbits; house the lacrimal sac |
| **Palatine bones** (2) | Form the posterior part of the hard palate and part of the nasal cavity |
| **Inferior nasal conchae** (2) | Curved bones projecting into the nasal cavity; aid in airflow regulation |
| **Vomer** (1) | Forms the inferior portion of the nasal septum |

---

## Associated Bones

| Bone | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Hyoid bone** | Not part of the skull proper; located in the neck; provides attachment for tongue and larynx muscles |
| **Auditory ossicles** (6 total – 3 per ear) | Malleus, incus, and stapes in each middle ear; sometimes included in skull bone count |

---

## Key Functions of Skull Bones

1. **Protection** – The cranial vault protects the brain; facial bones protect sensory organs (eyes, nose)
2. **Support** – Provides framework for facial structures and attachment points for muscles
3. **Housing** – Contains and protects special sense organs (hearing, balance, vision, smell)
4. **Openings** – Numerous foramina allow passage of cranial nerves, blood vessels, and the spinal cord

---

## Clinical Relevance

The **pterion** is a clinically important area where the frontal, parietal, temporal, and sphenoid bones meet. It overlies the middle meningeal artery, and fractures here can cause life-threatening **extradural hematoma**.

Sources:
1. https://www.kenhub.com/en/library/anatomy/the-skull
2. https://www.osmosis.org/learn/Bones_of_the_cranium
3. https://teachmeanatomy.info/head/osteology/skull/
4. https://www.numberanalytics.com/blog/skull-bones-anatomy-histology-explored
5. https://www.acibademhealthpoint.com/the-back-of-head-bones-understanding-cranial-anatomy/
6. https://anatomynote.com/the-human-skull-an-anatomical-masterpiece/
7. https://anatomy.co.uk/skull
